title: Конец утренним пробежкам  (An End to Morning Jogs)

segments.t: Relieved by Elena's honesty, Viktor Petrovich confesses in turn that he staged the urgent phone call from Lyova during their first run because he was about to pass out. Laughing together at their mutual pride, the two rival chefs happily shake hands on a pact: no more sports from this moment on.
Я вообще думаю, что вы откажетесь.
А со звонком вы здорово придумали.
С этого момента больше никакого спорта.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
Я вообще думаю, что вы откажетесь.
'I honestly thought that you would refuse.' Kostya chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'to refuse' to keep a polite distance. Nastya answers right away.
А со звонком вы здорово придумали.
'And that phone call trick you came up with was brilliant.' The grammar packs 'and' and 'to think up' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'All right, I will be right there.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'fine' before landing on 'to arrive'.
'Are you really leaving already, huh?' Notice how Russian expresses 'really' and 'and' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Kostya answers right away.
'What happened?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'what' before landing on 'to happen'.
'Yes, they are urgently calling me in to work.' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'urgently' in a few short words.
'Well then, tomorrow at the same place?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'already'. Nastya answers right away.
'At the exact same time?' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'time' in spoken Russian.
'Well, see you tomorrow.' Kostya anchors the line on 'come on', while 'tomorrow' completes the thought.
'Thank you for the company.' In Russian, the idea of 'thank you' flows naturally into 'company' without extra filler words. Kostya answers right away.
'All right, let us make a deal.' The grammar packs 'really?!' and 'we'll arrange' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
С этого момента больше никакого спорта.
'From this moment on, no more sports.' The grammar packs 'with' and 'sport' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I could not be happier to agree.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'yes' and finishing on 'glad'. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Я вообще думаю, что вы откажетесь.
А со звонком вы здорово придумали.
С этого момента больше никакого спорта.
